passage.title: A Blessing
passage.credit: —James Wright · “A Blessing” · from Above the River: The Complete Poems (1992), Wesleyan University Press

lines.text: Just off the highway to Rochester, Minnesota,
Twilight bounds softly forth on the grass.
And the eyes of those two Indian ponies
Darken with kindness.
They have come gladly out of the willows
To welcome my friend and me.
We step over the barbed wire into the pasture
Where they have been grazing all day, alone.
They ripple tensely, they can hardly contain their happiness
That we have come.
They bow shyly as wet swans. They love each other.
There is no loneliness like theirs.
At home once more,
They begin munching the young tufts of spring in the darkness.
I would like to hold the slenderer one in my arms,
For she has walked over to me
And nuzzled my left hand.
She is black and white,
Her mane falls wild on her forehead,
And the light breeze moves me to caress her long ear
That is delicate as the skin over a girl’s wrist.
Suddenly I realize
That if I stepped out of my body I would break
Into blossom.

questions.prompt: The act of stepping “over the barbed wire” (line 7) represents the

choices.text: entrance into a more natural world

questions.explanation: The speaker leaves the highway side and steps into a pasture with grazing ponies, grass, willows, and spring growth. Crossing the fence marks entry into the animals' natural setting.

questions.prompt: The statement “they ripple tensely” (line 9) reflects the ponies’ reaction to the
questions.explanation: The same line says the ponies can hardly contain their happiness “That we have come.” Their physical tension expresses excitement at the two visitors' arrival.

questions.prompt: The simile in line 11 suggests the ponies’
questions.explanation: “They bow shyly as wet swans” compares the ponies' movement to swans lowering their long necks. The comparison suggests graceful necks rather than feathers or coat texture.

questions.prompt: The poem is primarily developed through the use of

choices.text: imagery to describe an intense experience
exaggeration to enhance an interesting event

questions.explanation: Images of twilight, grass, the ponies' eyes, the nuzzled hand, and the delicate ear make the encounter vivid. That sensory imagery carries the speaker's intense feeling through the final blossom image.

questions.prompt: The title of the poem highlights the
questions.explanation: The speaker treats meeting and touching the ponies as a gift so powerful that it inspires the image of breaking “Into blossom.” The title names the importance of that encounter.
